absent: Hardware programming performed by hrtimer rearm and event device layer
Expiry iteration and callback dispatch inside queue runner
Time base update and next event selection algorithms
Tick oneshot switch, scheduler timer setup and low resolution handler internals
Remainder copyout formatting and signal freeze interactions for nanosleep
Process CPU clock sampling source beyond thread group helper
Broadcast and tick device lifecycle outside availability checks
Complete numeric values and full struct definitions for flags, modes and errors

findings.text: Public per CPU helper completes a previously requested timer rearm. It returns early when no deferral is pending, otherwise it holds the base guard while refreshing timekeeping and next expiry if an update was requested or reusing a cached expiry value, then requests hardware reprogramming in deferred mode.

Deferred rearm moves through request and completion states. The interrupt path marks deferral pending, parks the shared next expiry at its maximum sentinel and, depending on build variant, either caches the computed expiry and raises a thread flag for later completion or reprograms immediately in non deferred mode. The deferred helper consumes the pending mark and finishes reprogramming.

High resolution timer interrupt entry validates high resolution activity, counts the event, clears device next event bookkeeping, updates the per CPU time base under lock, triggers timer softirq when soft expiry is due, runs hard expiry queues, then recomputes next expiry with bounded retries before unlocking and delegating rearm.

The interrupt gives at most three passes when the recomputed next expiry is already in the past, counting retries. Persistent overrun is treated as a hang with elapsed time since entry retained as maximum observed hang duration, hang count incremented and hang detected flag set.

Low resolution timer processing entry exits when high resolution is active. It otherwise consults the oneshot change helper and may switch to high resolution, or under lock refreshes the base, activates timer softirq if soft expiry elapsed and runs hard queues.

The scheduler clock check clears a per CPU pending flag and reports no change when unset, when nohz mode is already set, or when timekeeping or hardware oneshot support is unavailable. When nohz is disallowed it requests a mode switch, otherwise it attempts transition to nohz and reports no further change. A header variant always reports no change.

Oneshot readiness requires a present per CPU event device advertising oneshot capability. Devices that need no broadcast stop in deep idle are immediately usable, otherwise readiness defers to broadcast device state read once and tested for oneshot support, with header fallbacks reducing to a global possible predicate that is true in one configuration and false in another.

Transition to nohz low resolution handling is a no operation when the global nohz enable is clear or when oneshot switch fails, otherwise it recycles the scheduler timer for shared high resolution handling. An alternate build provides an empty operation.
High resolution suitability is determined by a seqlock protected read of the monotonic clock source flags testing the valid for high resolution bit, retried on concurrent writer.

Per CPU timer base mutation and expiry computation are serialized by the base raw spinlock held with interrupts saved across base update, soft expiry handling, queue execution and rearm decision in both interrupt and low resolution paths, while deferred completion uses a scoped guard on the same lock.

Nanosleep sleepers bind a wakeup callback and the current task at setup, with on stack setup adding debug tracking. Start enforces hard delivery on realtime builds when the sleeper is marked hard, and treats immediate expiry as task cleared plus running state. Wakeup detaches the task exactly once, wakes it if present and requests no restart.

On realtime builds a sleeper inherits hard interrupt expiry only for callers in realtime or deadline policy without an explicit soft request, preserving low latency for privileged realtime use while keeping untrusted mass wakeups in soft context for latency control.

Nanosleep blocking loops through sleep start, schedule while the sleeper still owns a task, timer cancel and conversion to absolute mode for subsequent passes until task detachment or signal. It then restores running state, returns success on expiry, copies remaining time when the restart block expects output and remaining time is positive, otherwise reports restart block continuation.

Relative and absolute sleeps create an on stack sleeper with caller slack tolerance and delegate to the blocking loop, destroying the object on exit. Relative sleeps that require restart record clock identity, expiry and a restart function for later resumption, while absolute sleeps map restart continuation to a no hand restart error. Restart rehydrates the sleeper from saved clock and expiry and reenters the loop in absolute mode.

Native and 32 bit nanosleep entries copy a user duration, reject copy failure and invalid values, initialize the current restart block to no restart with a type reflecting whether a remainder pointer was supplied, then invoke a monotonic relative sleep over the converted duration.

User duration fetch copies a fixed kernel shape and reports fault on failure, masking nanoseconds to low bits in compat mode. The old 32 bit path copies natively when 64 bit time is in use, otherwise converts separate second and nanosecond fields. Nanosecond to timespec conversion normalizes positive values by division and negative values with borrow so seconds round toward earlier time and nanoseconds stay non negative.

Per CPU timer preparation links every clock base to its CPU base, initializes per base sequence protection against the base lock and empties its queue, then records CPU identity and expiry lock state. Starting clears active masks and hang state, nulls next timer tracking, parks expiries at maximum, clears softirq activation and marks the CPU online.
Early initialization prepares and starts timer state for the boot processor and registers the timer softirq handler.

Timer migration on CPU teardown acquires old then new base locks in nested order under global serialization, moves every queued timer by removing it in enqueued state to avoid disappearing to concurrent observers, retargeting its base and requeueing absolute without immediate hardware reprogram, then notifies the survivor to reevaluate next event before marking the old base offline.

Interval timer remaining queries use an internal remaining helper with race safe handling where active timers with elapsed remainder report one microsecond and inactive report zero. CPU timers sample thread group execution under signal lock and report tick granularity when expiry already passed, otherwise remaining execution, alongside stored interval.

Thread group CPU time sampling warns when posix timers are inactive, atomically reads user, system and total runtime counters and derives profiling as user plus system, virtual as user alone and scheduled as total runtime.

Interval timer query dispatches real time to hrtimer remaining plus stored increment under signal lock and virtual or profiling to CPU sampling, rejecting other selectors. Native and compat outputs translate intervals and values from nanoseconds to seconds plus microseconds and report fault when user copy fails.
Compat interval value layout pairs an interval member and a value member, each holding seconds and microseconds fields for user transfer.

Real interval rearm proceeds only when the timer is not queued and a non zero increment is stored, advancing expiry relative to now by the increment and restarting. Expiry traces the event and delivers a private alarm signal to the thread group leader without requesting restart.

CPU interval update converts new and old specs between timespec and nanoseconds, adds tick granularity to positive new values, delegates absolute conversion and earliest expiry maintenance to the process timer helper, stores new expiry and increment under signal lock, traces the resulting state and returns prior values when requested. The process helper ignores out of range clock ids, samples group time, converts stored absolute old value to relative and relative new value to absolute, refreshes the earliest cache when earlier and marks posix timer dependency.
Interval and CPU timer get and set paths serialize access to per process expiry and increment storage with the signal handler spinlock held with interrupts disabled.

Per CPU timer base observed state includes a lock, array of clock bases, active base mask, high resolution flag, online flag, CPU number, hang detection flag with retry hang and max hang accounting, event count, next timer and softirq next timer references, next expiry and softirq expiry sentinels, softirq activation flag and deferred rearm pending flag with needs update indicator plus cached expiry.

Sleeper state pairs a timer object with an owning task pointer and hard delivery marker. Nanosleep restart state carries a type distinguishing none native and compat, a clock identity, an expiry instant and a user remainder destination in native or compat form.

Maximum time value denotes absence of next event and of softirq expiry. Monotonic clock with relative mode selects nanosleep duration interpretation, with absolute mode used for retries and restart. Interval selectors distinguish real virtual and profiling timers, with invalid selectors rejected.

Parking next expiry at maximum while running queues prevents remote enqueue from interfering with local expiry processing, while local requeue remains permitted. Parking soft expiry at maximum before raising softirq avoids duplicate activation. Compat duration fetch discards high nanosecond bits, so callers must not rely on full width there.

Exported timer mode and time conversion helpers expose oneshot availability, high resolution suitability and user time copying plus nanosecond conversion for use by mode switching, sleep and interval paths.
